resumen: Sujeto u objeto: si who/what es el sujeto, la pregunta no lleva auxiliar: Who phoned you?; si es el objeto, sí lo lleva: Who did you phone?

Question tags: afirmativa → coletilla negativa y al revés, con el mismo auxiliar: You've finished, haven't you? Casos especiales: I'm late, aren't I? · Let's go, shall we? · Don't forget, will you? · Nobody called, did they? · He never calls, does he?
Preguntas indirectas: tras Could you tell me…? / Do you know…? / I wonder… se usa el orden de la afirmativa y sin do: Could you tell me where the station is? Para sí/no, if o whether.
So / Neither: «yo también» = So + auxiliar + sujeto (So do I, So am I); «yo tampoco» = Neither/Nor + auxiliar afirmativo + sujeto (Neither have I).
Comparativos y superlativos: irregulares good – better – best, bad – worse – worst, far – further – furthest. Se intensifican con much / far / a lot o slightly / a bit, nunca con very: far cheaper.
As…as y multiplicadores: not as big as, twice as big as, three times as fast as; than va solo con el comparativo. Doble comparativo: The more you practise, the better you get.
So / Such: so + adjetivo o adverbio (so tired, so many); such (a) + (adjetivo) + sustantivo (such a long day, such good news).
Too / Enough: too va antes del adjetivo (too expensive); enough va después del adjetivo y antes del sustantivo (old enough, enough time).

preguntas.q: Mark phoned someone last night, and you want to know who that person was. Which question do you ask?
preguntas.x: Aquí who es el objeto (Mark llamó a alguien), así que se necesita auxiliar: Who did Mark phone? Who phoned Mark? es gramatical, pero pregunta por la persona que llamó a Mark; y tras did el verbo va en forma base, no en pasado.

preguntas.q: Everyone looks upset. What ___ at the meeting this morning?
preguntas.x: Cuando what es el sujeto, la pregunta no lleva auxiliar: What happened? Happen no tiene voz pasiva, así que was happened es imposible, y did it happen añade un sujeto que sobra (calco de «¿qué pasó?»).

preguntas.q: That was the ___ film I've ever seen. I left the cinema after twenty minutes.
preguntas.x: Bad es irregular: bad – worse – the worst. Con the + I've ever seen se necesita el superlativo; worse es el comparativo, y baddest o most bad no existen en el inglés estándar.

preguntas.q: A: I'm really tired after that exam. B: So ___ I. Let's go home.
preguntas.x: Para decir «yo también» se repite el auxiliar de la primera frase: I'm tired → So am I. So do I responde a un verbo en presente simple sin auxiliar (I like it → So do I), y did cambiaría el tiempo.

preguntas.q: Excuse me, could you tell me where ___?
d: the nearest cash machine it is
does the nearest cash machine is
preguntas.x: En una pregunta indirecta (Could you tell me…?, Do you know…?) la segunda parte va en orden de afirmativa: sujeto + verbo. Where is the nearest cash machine es el orden de la pregunta directa y no se repite aquí.

preguntas.q: It was ___ lovely afternoon that we decided to have our class outside.
preguntas.x: Such a/an va delante de un sustantivo contable singular, con o sin adjetivo: such a lovely afternoon. So va solo con un adjetivo o adverbio (It was so lovely that…), y such sin artículo solo sirve con plurales o incontables (such lovely weather).

preguntas.q: The second test was ___ harder than the first one; almost nobody passed it.
preguntas.x: Un comparativo se intensifica con far, much o a lot (y con slightly o a bit si la diferencia es pequeña): far harder. Very y too no modifican comparativos, y more harder duplica el comparativo.

preguntas.q: I'm on the list for Friday's workshop, ___? I signed up last week.
preguntas.x: Después de I am en afirmativo, la coletilla es la forma irregular aren't I? (la muy formal es am I not?). Isn't it es el calco del «¿no es cierto?» del español, y am not I tiene el orden equivocado.

preguntas.q: Nobody has replied to the group chat yet, ___?
preguntas.x: Nobody ya hace negativa la oración, así que la coletilla va en afirmativo, y con nobody / somebody / everyone se usa they: have they? Haven't they sería una doble negación.

preguntas.q: A: I haven't finished the essay yet. B: ___ I. Shall we work on it together?
preguntas.x: «Yo tampoco» tras una frase negativa: Neither/Nor + auxiliar en afirmativo + sujeto: Neither have I. Neither haven't I tiene doble negación, So have I respondería a una afirmativa y either solo va al final: I haven't either.

preguntas.q: Renting a flat in the city centre is ___ renting one in the suburbs.
preguntas.x: Para multiplicar se usa twice / three times + as + adjetivo + as: twice as expensive as. As…as no se mezcla con than, que solo acompaña al comparativo (more expensive than).

preguntas.q: Don't forget to back up your files before the update, ___?
preguntas.x: Con imperativos la coletilla se forma con will, no con do: tras Don't… la única posible es will you? (Don't forget, will you?). Do you y don't you preguntarían por una costumbre en vez de suavizar una petición.

preguntas.a: Could you tell me when the next train to Oxford leaves?
d: Could you tell me when does the next train to Oxford leave?
Could you tell me when leaves the next train to Oxford?
Could you tell me when will the next train to Oxford leave?
preguntas.x: En la pregunta indirecta desaparece el auxiliar do/does y se usa el orden sujeto + verbo: when the next train leaves. Conservar does o invertir el verbo (when leaves, when will the train) es copiar el orden de la pregunta directa.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “The meeting room was too small for all the participants.”
preguntas.a: The meeting room wasn't big enough for all the participants.
d: The meeting room wasn't enough big for all the participants.
The meeting room wasn't small enough for all the participants.
The meeting room was big enough for all the participants.
preguntas.x: Too + adjetivo (más de la cuenta) equivale a not + adjetivo contrario + enough: too small = not big enough. Enough va después del adjetivo, nunca antes (big enough, no enough big).

preguntas.a: Let's leave the rest of the agenda for Monday, shall we?
d: He never answers emails on time, doesn't he?
Don't be late for the interview, do you?
There's no milk left, isn't there?
preguntas.x: Tras Let's… la coletilla es shall we?. Las demás fallan: never y no ya hacen negativa la oración, así que piden coletilla afirmativa (does he?, is there?), y tras un imperativo negativo va will you?.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “Marta isn't nearly as confident as her sister.”
preguntas.a: Her sister is much more confident than Marta.
d: Her sister is almost as confident as Marta.
Marta is nearly as confident as her sister.
Marta is much more confident than her sister.
preguntas.x: Not nearly as… as significa «ni de lejos tan… como»: la diferencia es grande, así que equivale a much more… than con los sujetos invertidos. Nearly as confident as (casi tan seguro como) expresa justo lo contrario: una diferencia pequeña.

preguntas.q: The longer we wait to book, ___.
preguntas.a: the more expensive the tickets will be
d: the tickets will be more expensive
the more the tickets will be expensive
more expensive the tickets will be
preguntas.x: El doble comparativo lleva the + comparativo al principio de las dos partes, con el adjetivo pegado a the more: the more expensive the tickets will be. Si falta the o el adjetivo se queda al final (the more the tickets will be expensive), la estructura se rompe.

preguntas.q: ___ was the demand for tickets that the website crashed within minutes.
preguntas.x: En registro formal se antepone such con inversión: Such was the demand that… (= The demand was so great that…). So necesitaría un adjetivo (So great was the demand…), y such a exige un sustantivo contable justo detrás.
